prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a narrow garden path running forward between rose bushes, with the plants on both sides generally about 0.3–1.5 m from the camera wearer and the visible person roughly 1–2 m ahead; brighter regions indicate that the person and some nearby foliage are closer than the dark, more distant path and background. Across the five frames, the person shifts from the upper-right area toward the centre-right and becomes much larger and brighter, indicating that the camera wearer approaches to roughly 0.5–1 m, while the final frame also contains a very near, partly out-of-view arm or hand at the lower right, likely within arm's reach. The person remains in front of the camera wearer, with bushes to their left and right and the ground below; their changing silhouette suggests some turning, but facing direction and gaze are not reliably resolved by depth alone. This map makes near-versus-far ordering and the narrowing free space along the path clearer than RGB, but foliage boundaries are blurred, the ground has an implausibly smooth depth gradient, and the person's estimated depth is inconsistent in places, so metric distances are approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates one person ahead from the surrounding path and vegetation, placing them near the upper-right in the first two frames, nearer the centre-right in the next two, and very large on the right in the fifth frame as separation from the camera wearer decreases from roughly 1–2 m to about 0.5–1 m. The increasing mask size reveals the approach and shows that the person's body becomes progressively more cropped by the top and right image boundaries; in the final frame, a second small person-labelled region at the far lower right corresponds to the camera wearer's partly visible near arm or hand, within roughly 0.2–0.5 m. The map clarifies which pixels belong to the person despite overlap with dense plants, but it provides no masks for the rose bushes, flowers, path, water, or other objects, so their separations and reachability must come from RGB and depth. It also cannot reliably establish gaze or exact facing direction, and the final camera-wearer limb is mislabeled as a separate person while portions of the main person's limbs are missing or merged.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only sparse yellow body joints for the person in the third and fourth frames, at centre-right and then slightly farther right, supporting that the person is upright about 0.7–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer and growing nearer between those frames. The visible joint arrangement mainly traces one side of the lower body and does not include a reliable head, torso, arms, or eyes, so it cannot determine whether the person faces or looks toward the camera wearer, nor whether either person's hands are within reach. No skeleton is recovered in frames one, two, or five, even though RGB and segmentation show the person there; the likely causes are small scale and plant occlusion early, followed by severe close-range cropping in the last frame. Compared with RGB, the map makes a few limb locations and their slight rightward motion easier to isolate, but its missing joints, absence of magenta hand detections, and frame-to-frame dropout make detailed body orientation, occlusion structure, and interpersonal distance unreliable.
